- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2% lagged momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; avoid overfitting to recent history — use 10-day sentiment-weighted smoothing instead.
